scope: Six additions from the complete priority audit checked against primary texts. Existing 25 entries retained, not exhaustively reverified in this pass. No mathematical theorem modified.
provenance_note: A scan of an original article is primary textual evidence even when served by an archival mirror. Failed DOI resolution is recorded separately from successful access to an original text.

metadata.title: A bound for error-correcting codes
metadata.journal: IBM Journal of Research and Development

primary_sources.type: original published article scan, archival mirror

claims.claim: Classical binary linear-code length bound and residual-code argument underlie the truncated redundancy inequality in P1 Lemma 2.1.

references.mapping_to_p1: For r>=t, the remaining r-t terms in the full Griesmer sum are at least one. Subtracting r yields the truncated redundancy bound.
limitations: The arithmetic lower bound on minimum relation weight and its use at logarithmic length are separate P1 arguments.
DOI landing page was not accessible in this session; the identifier from the audit is retained without claiming its resolver was validated.

claims.claim: The first-excluded-prefix identity is an exact specialization of formula (*).

references.mapping_to_p1: Set l(S)=S on the hereditary retained class; otherwise choose the first excluded prefix. Fixed sets are the class and its ordered boundary. Compatible sets are empty on the class and the strict suffix beyond max I on the boundary.
limitations: The published year is 1997, despite later arXiv deposition.
Attribution concerns the finite identity; P1 estimates of the arithmetic boundary remain separate.

metadata.title: Concentration of points on two and three dimensional modular hyperbolas and applications

claims.claim: Lemma 4 supplies a subpower count for x^2-Ay^2=E with nonsquare A and coefficients/variables polynomially bounded in M; Proposition 1 allows a general quadratic equation with nonsquare discriminant.

references.mapping_to_p1: Multiply au^2-bv^2=h by a, setting x=au, A=ab and E=ah. For square ab use the factorization/divisor argument with h nonzero.
limitations: Nonsquare discriminant is an explicit hypothesis of Proposition 1.
The published title includes 'of'; arXiv v2's title omits it.
The exponent O(1) defining the coefficient/variable range is fixed.

metadata.title: Products of consecutive integers with unusual anatomy

claims.claim: Lemma 2.10 bounds the number of positive integer solutions to an^2+h=bm^2 with n<=x, positive a,b and nonzero h of polynomial size, by x^{o(1)}.

references.mapping_to_p1: Directly comparable recent formulation; the sign of h can be reversed to match the P1 convention.
limitations: The proof expressly credits Cilleruelo–Garaev Lemma 4 and Proposition 1.
This is a supplementary formulation, not a replacement for the earlier attribution.

metadata.title: Discrete approximations for sums of m-dependent random variables
metadata.journal: ALEA, Latin American Journal of Probability and Mathematical Statistics
metadata.version_used: published journal text; arXiv:1301.7196v3 listed as supplementary access

claims.claim: The quadratic Poisson correction and its convolution exponential are compared; the former bound contains R_0^2 and the latter does not.

references.mapping_to_p1: Their Gamma_1 is the mean and Gamma_2 is half variance minus half mean, corresponding to mu and alpha/2.
limitations: Nonnegative integer summands are 1-dependent (or m-dependent before grouping), with explicit factorial-moment and positivity conditions.
Long-range arithmetic dependence in P1 is not covered by direct application.
No numerical constant or rate is imported from this theorem.

metadata.title: Mod-phi convergence: Approximation of discrete measures and harmonic analysis on the torus

primary_sources.type: published journal text in official archive

claims.claim: Theorem 3.11 gives asymptotic total-variation expressions for mod-phi approximation schemes with parameter tending to infinity, under residue regularity H2 and a third-moment condition on the reference law.

references.mapping_to_p1: Context for extracting a distance equivalent from the leading residual term, not an applied theorem.
limitations: P1 keeps its Poisson means bounded away from zero and infinity.
The source defines d_TV as the full l1 norm, twice P1's usual probability total-variation distance.

public_scope: Credit classical code, lace and quadratic-count tools.
Preserve earlier Paper C v3 Poisson theorem and 2:3 channel attribution.
Keep optimality attached to the exact quadratic reference and fixed channel heights.
